title: Quadratic lower levels: exact values, gradients, and vector products.
summary: Solve the bilevel problem $\min_x\Phi(x)$, where $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^*(x))$ and $y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_y g(x,y)$ is the unique global lower-level solution. The upper- and lower-level variables are $x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ and $y\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$. Seek approximate stationarity of the reduced objective under the declared criterion and guarantee; assumptions on $f$, $g$, and $\Phi$ are specified separately.

model.instance: (f,g,x0,y0) and declared oracle law; dimensions are arbitrary finite and minimax is over them

assumptions.description: Assume $g(x,y)=\tfrac12y^\top Hy+x^\top Jy+b^\top y$, $H=H^\top$, $\mu I\preceq H\preceq LI$, and $\|J\|\le L$, with fixed unknown coefficients. The function $g$ is strongly convex in $y$ but need not be jointly convex.

The class inclusion in Definition 2.3 still requires $\nabla g$ to be $L$-Lipschitz jointly in $(x,y)$. Equivalently, its constant joint Hessian $\bigl[\begin{smallmatrix}0&J\\J^\top&H\end{smallmatrix}\bigr]$ has operator norm at most $L$. Separate bounds on H and J alone do not ensure the same L.
The full gradient of $f$ is jointly $L$-Lipschitz. Nonconvexity is allowed. No finite global Lipschitz or norm bound is imposed on the values of $f$ or on $f_y$.
$\Phi(0)-\inf_x\Phi(x)\le\Delta$, with upper-level initial point zero. The lower-level initial point may also be zero, but no additional uniform distance bound is imposed.

model.parameter_domain_description: Each regularity assumption applies to its stated variable blocks, full Euclidean query domain, and norm. Samplewise conditions apply only when explicitly declared.
model.outer_geometry: The reduced objective may be nonconvex. Its differentiability or local Lipschitz regularity is specified by the model and accuracy measure.

oracle.query_domain_description: Upper and lower points may be selected adaptively throughout their declared Euclidean spaces. Each operation specifies direction dimensions and control over samples or indices.
oracle.native_source_protocol: The bundled O_fo interface in Definition 2.4 returns f,g and both full gradients in one call. This specification charges four primitive operations, so four calls simulate it. Definition 2.6 adds Jv and Hv to O_hvp, requiring at most six primitive calls. Hessian-vector products are charged.
description_paragraphs: Public inputs are dimension, target accuracy, the model's budgets, and the initial point. The original functions, their lower-level solutions, and the reduced objective are hidden. Queries are restricted to the stated interfaces; inner optima and undeclared derivatives are not available for free.
The map $(x,y)\mapsto f(x,y)$ is returned exactly, with no additional random noise.
The map $(x,y)\mapsto\nabla f(x,y)$ is returned exactly, with no additional random noise.
The map $(x,y)\mapsto g(x,y)$ is returned exactly, with no additional random noise.
The response is $(x,y)\longmapsto \nabla g(x,y)$, returned exactly with no additional stochastic noise.
The map $(x,y,v)\mapsto g_{xy}(x,y)v$ is returned exactly, with no additional random noise.
$(x,y,v)\longmapsto g_{yy}(x,y)v$. The stated response is exact, with no additional random noise.

The bundled interface $O_{\rm fo}$ in Definition 2.4 returns $f,g,\nabla f,\nabla g$ in one call. Here it is split into four charged primitive operations, so one source call costs four. Definition 2.6 adds cross-derivative action $Jv$ and lower-Hessian action $Hv$ to interface $O_{\rm hvp}$; at most six primitive calls simulate it.

metric.normalization: The tolerance $\varepsilon$ is on the gradient-norm scale; this contract requires a deterministic norm bound.
metric.finiteness_conditions: Guaranteed by the model and the associated differentiability result, not inferred from an oracle-order label alone.
description_paragraphs: The base error is $\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat{x})\|_2$, with $\varepsilon$ always specified on the gradient-norm scale. Gradient norm and squared gradient norm remain distinct.

In this unconstrained model with a strongly convex lower level, $
abla\Phi(x)=
abla_x f(x,y^*)-g_{xy}(x,y^*)g_{yy}(x,y^*)^{-1}
abla_y f(x,y^*)$, where $g_{xy}=\mathrm{D}_y
abla_x g$ and $g_{yy}=\mathrm{D}_y
abla_y g$, and $y^*$ denotes $y^*(x)$. The identity defines the hypergradient without granting additional query access.

algorithms.internal_computation: This model counts only oracle resources. Arithmetic, linear algebra, and storage applied to received responses are free. Any extra hidden-function gradient, HVP/JVP, value, or inner-solve response must be obtained through a declared, charged operation.
algorithms.parallelism: sequential adaptive calls; simultaneous batch calls count separately
description_paragraphs: Algorithms are deterministic and may use arbitrary measurable adaptive queries, stopping, and postprocessing. Outputs may be unqueried, deterministically selected historical points, or admissible averages. No span or zero-respecting restriction applies. Queries are sequential; each response in a batch is charged. Internal arithmetic, linear algebra, and storage are free, with no separate work, memory, or communication budget.

aggregation_order: For every admissible instance, the deterministic output has true gradient norm at most ε.
guarantees.quantifier_order: A single algorithm family, depending only on public budgets and the interaction history, must meet the target for every admissible function and oracle law. Minimax quantifiers are infimum over algorithms followed by supremum over instances; the algorithm is not selected separately for each hidden instance.
description_paragraphs: Choose an algorithm using the public parameters, then require $\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat{x})\|_2\le\varepsilon$ for every admissible instance and oracle law. The guarantee is deterministic and applies instance by instance.
